## The claim

P4-8: the RRF consensus places the confirmed BUB1B pair first among the callset's biallelic pairs when catalogue-adjacent lanes are excluded.

**Prediction if true.** In docs/iteration4/report.md section 3, the catalogue-free row's confirmed-pair RRF rank is 1.

**What would refute it.** The confirmed pair's catalogue-free RRF rank is outside the top 5 — the disagreement table then names the lanes responsible.

| 1 | proposed | — | — |
| 2 | refuted | 0.02 | Predicted rank 1, pre-registered 'outside the top 5' as refuting, measured 20,639 of 52,012. There is no reading of that as a near miss. The refutation clause asks the disagreement table to name the lanes responsible, and the honest answer is that it names the wrong thing: all 90 disagreement rows are the same benign shape (a splice-window allele that missense models find unremarkable). What sank the pair is abstention, not disagreement — AlphaMissense, ESM1b and REVEL are missense-only, the pair is half stop_gained, and none of the three could rank it, so the fused score is exactly 1/(60+11,980), SpliceAI's reciprocal rank alone. Plan §10 R9 named this failure mode before the iteration began and entries 114, 119 and 129 tracked it from consequence classes to coverage to an absent rank. The revision is a lane that scores a nonsense allele (GPN-MSA). What the run did establish: three models of different provenance place the pair's missense allele in the top 0.47 %, 2.52 % and 2.59 % of what they scored. Entry 130. |
